# Commonwealth Utility Audit

> Independent utility bill auditing firm serving Virginia and Washington, DC. It recomputes every line of a building's electric, gas and water bills against the meter readings and the utility's published tariff, recovers overcharges from the utility, and offers optional monthly bill monitoring. The audit is free; the only charge is 33% of refunds actually received (20% for monthly-analysis clients).

## Key facts
- Legal name: Commonwealth Utility Audit LLC (Virginia). Founder and principal: Zak Zaloom.
- Area served: Virginia and Washington, DC.
- Utilities covered: any electric, gas, water or sewer utility in Virginia and Washington, DC; bills are recomputed from each utility's own published rates.
- Clients: owner-paid apartment and student housing communities, commercial buildings, higher education and healthcare campuses, government buildings.
- Pricing: back-audit of 24 to 36 months of bills is free. Recovery fee is 33% of refunds and credits actually received (20% for clients on monthly analysis), invoiced after the credit posts. No fee if nothing is recovered and none on future savings. Monthly analysis (the No-Surprise Utility Program) is optional: $150 per building per month where utilities are passed to residents, $300 owner-paid up to $300,000 a year in utilities, $500 above that, Full Service from $750; first three months for the price of one; value guarantee; from month four billed monthly (cancellable on 30 days' notice), quarterly, or yearly in advance (12 months for the price of 10), with quarterly and yearly running to the end of the period paid for.
- Apartment and student housing owners: https://commonwealthutilityaudit.com/apartments-and-student-housing.html (owner's share and resident billing checked monthly).
- Turnaround: written findings within 7 days of receiving the bills; every finding shows its arithmetic and tariff basis; the client approves each claim before it is filed.
- What is needed to start: 24 months of bills for one building, or a signed letter of authorization. No utility portal passwords are held.
- Independence: does not sell or broker energy supply and takes no compensation from utilities or suppliers. Works alongside utility billing and submetering companies rather than replacing them.
- Contact: zak@commonwealthutilityaudit.com

## Typical findings
- Demand charges billed on a misread or doubled meter reading
- Accounts on the wrong rate schedule
- Long runs of estimated reads followed by a catch-up bill
- Late fees on bills the utility later corrected
- Sales tax on tax-exempt accounts
- Duplicate charges after a meter replacement
- Sewer charged on water that never reaches the sewer (cooling towers, pools, irrigation), which a deduct meter can stop
